body:
## Summary

The gateway stores and returns **no object metadata beyond byte size**: no `ETag` (on the `PutObject` response or `GetObject`), no `Content-Type` (GET is always `application/octet-stream`), no `Last-Modified`, no `x-amz-meta-*`. Many SDKs validate the `ETag` and round-trip `Content-Type`; its absence breaks integrity checks and content typing.

**Current behavior:** PUT returns an empty body with no ETag (`crates/gateway-s3/src/lib.rs:315,352-357`); GET sets only `Content-Length` + a hardcoded `Content-Type` (`:326-329`). The inode carries `size` + `chunk_map` only (`crates/server/src/lib.rs`).

## Scope for Alpha
- Decide and record the **object-metadata model**: which fields live on the inode (`etag`, `content_type`, `created`/`modified`, optional `user_metadata`). This is the design foundation the other object ops build on.
- Compute + persist an `ETag` on PUT (the content digest already streamed by `HashingSource` is a natural basis; note S3's multipart-ETag convention for #multipart).
- Persist `Content-Type` from the PUT request; return it on GET/HEAD.
- Return `ETag` on the `PutObject` response and on GET/HEAD; add `Last-Modified`.

## Acceptance
- `PutObject` response carries an `ETag`; `GetObject` returns the same `ETag`, the stored `Content-Type`, and `Last-Modified`.
- Round-trip through aws-cli/boto3 with ETag validation enabled succeeds.

Blocks: HeadObject, multipart (ETag-of-parts). Part of the 0.1-Alpha S3 completion epic.
